newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday showed spending in Australian stores has risen for a fourth successive month in August, but the retail sector still appears shaky, with analysts saying any improvement in sales in the near future could be capped by slow employment and wages growth. Page 3.

In a veiled reference to the recent spate of racist comments in public debate in Australia, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad yesterday warned Australia against making "funny remarks" about Malaysians - a sign that Australia's relations with Malaysia are strained due to the resurgence of anti-Asian sentiment in Australia. Page 3.

In an effort to control public debate over the sensitive issue of media ownership in Australia, the Howard Government has moved to fast-track its media review and plans to release draft legislation for public comment with a bill introduced into Parliament in early 1997 - a move which will see telecommunications companies, Internet service providers and magazine publishers being brought within extended cross-media ownership rules. Page 5.

In a submission to the Mansfield review, Australian Broadcasting Commission managing director Brian Johns revealed the group's most radical plans yet for overhauling its services and structure in response to the Howard Government's review of its role, allowing for the first time independent producers to compete with ABC production for TV programmes other than news and current affairs. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a bid to prevent a "media circus", Communications Minister Richard Alston yesterday committed the federal government to abandoning its promised full public inquiry into cross-media ownership in favour of an internal review to assess whether the rules sould be changed by 1997, which will include the current ad hoc rules covering foreign ownership and control of the media. Page 1.

Speaking in Melbourne yesterday, Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett made a strong call for a broad-based consumption tax, saying there was a distinct need for broad-based taxation reform, as Opposition Treasury spokesman Gareth Evans argued Australia is under-taxed. Page 1.

The Howard Government revealed yesterday it will support those wanting the High Court's landmark 1994 Theophanous and Stephens free political speech judgments overturned. In two separate cases, the Victorian Government and former New Zealand Prime Minister David Lange have asked the High Court to reopen and overrule the judgments decided by a 4-3 majority in 1994. Page 1.

Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron told The Australian yesterday cancellation of funding to indigenous organisations identified as abusing federal grants will justify the cost of a A$1 million audit into the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As a number of leading barristers sought to intervene on behalf of the media in a High Court case that may overturn its own free speech rulings, the federal government has announced it will seek to overturn the High Court's historic ruling to enshrine theright to free political speech in the constitution, despite Prime Minister John Howard's endorsement of its "cardinal" importance to democracy. Page 1.

Speaking on Melbourne radio yesterday, Shadow Treasurer Gareth Evans made a surprise admission when he advocated an increase in federal revenue to address Australia's low-tax status, revealing tax rises would be likely under Labor. Page 1.

New South Wales Transport Minister Brian Langton has defended the new taxi law which penalises cab drivers who carry babies under a year old without a capsule, even though they appear to be unworkable with parents forced to travel on buses or lie to taxi drivers about their child's age. Page 1.

Five pre-schoolers who were allegedly beaten, pushed, force-fed and restrained with straps during incidents at a Sydney preschool over several months, were yesterday receiving psychological assessments by the New South Wales Department of Community Service to determine their individual counselling and support needs. Page 3.
THE AGE

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett plans to radically change the role of the state governor to include a brief to develop Victoria's business interests overseas. Kennett revealed yesterday that the successor to current governor Richard McGarvie will take the traditionally ceremonial role to "a different plateau". Page A1.

After a breakdown in financial negotiations between Sky Channel and Tabcorp last night, Victoria's 290 TAB agencies will be blacked out from national racing television service today. The dispute between the organisations escalated when Sky Channel rejected Tabcorp's latest offer which would have seen an increase in fees of 120 percent to receive the Sky signal. Page A1.

Parking fines in Victoria will increase by 66 percent for some offences as the State Government attempts to curb "irresponsible drivers" on Victorian roads. Roads Minister Geoff Craige said the increases - the first in six years - have been prompted by a decline in the effectiveness of current penalties, with the highest fine bracket now A$100 up from A$60. Page A1.

The federal government has rejected an inquiry into media ownership, fearing it would turn into a "media circus". As an alternative, the government will release its own draft legislation early next year after accepting public submissions. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
